answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through graph-theoretic trust routing. Verified agents sign mutual trust edges, isolating synthetic identities behind sparse bridge bottlenecks. Validating an agent via random-walk mixing forces attackers to incur the verifiable cost of securing scarce, genuine peer relationships per identity. However, against a raven backdrop of collusive traffic, the crystal rigidity of static cut thresholds risks wrongfully excluding honest newcomers.
